questions.enonce_markdown:
Define the following terms giving an example in each case:

(i) Cell  (ii) Tissue. *(3, 3 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) A **cell** is the basic structural and functional unit of all living organisms. *Example:* a red blood cell (or a nerve cell, a palisade cell).

(ii) A **tissue** is a group of similar cells, with the same origin, that work together to perform a particular function. *Example:* muscle tissue (or epithelial tissue, xylem tissue).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Describe the structure of the following muscular tissues;

(i) Skeletal muscle (ii) Smooth muscle (iii) Cardiac muscle. *(3, 3, 3 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Skeletal muscle**: made of long, cylindrical, unbranched fibres, each fibre being a multinucleate cell with many nuclei lying just under the cell membrane (sarcolemma). The fibres show clear cross-striations (light and dark bands) because of the arrangement of actin and myosin filaments. It is attached to bones by tendons and contains many mitochondria.

(ii) **Smooth muscle**: made of short, spindle-shaped cells with tapering ends. Each cell has a single, central nucleus. There are no cross-striations. The cells are arranged in sheets or layers in the walls of the alimentary canal, blood vessels and bladder.

(iii) **Cardiac muscle**: made of short, cylindrical fibres that are branched and interconnected, each with one central nucleus. The fibres show faint cross-striations and are joined end to end by special junctions called **intercalated discs**. It is found only in the wall of the heart and has many mitochondria.

questions.enonce_markdown: In tabular form, distinguish between mitosis and meiosis. *(5 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
| Mitosis | Meiosis |
|---|---|
| Occurs in body (somatic) cells | Occurs in the reproductive organs (testes and ovaries) to form gametes |
| One division only | Two successive divisions (meiosis I and II) |
| Produces two daughter cells | Produces four daughter cells |
| Daughter cells have the same chromosome number as the parent cell (diploid, $2n$) | Daughter cells have half the chromosome number (haploid, $n$) |
| Daughter cells are genetically identical to the parent cell | Daughter cells are genetically different (variation) |
| No crossing over; homologous chromosomes do not pair | Crossing over occurs between paired homologous chromosomes |
| Responsible for growth, repair and replacement of cells | Responsible for the formation of gametes |
